Judgment
.
Heard Mr. A. W. Paunikar, learned Counsel for the Appellant, Mr. P. S. Mirache, learned Counsel for the Respondent Nos.1 and 2.
None appeared for the Respondent No.3, though served.
2. By this Appeal, the Appellant has challenged the Judgment and Order dated 1/1/2020 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Nagpur in Claim Petition No. 416/2003.

3. On perusal of the Appeal Memo, it appears that the main ground of challenge in the present Appeal is that the policy of the offending vehicle, which is placed on record, was for the period from 14/9/2001 upto midnight on 13/9/2002.

The accident occurred on 16/4/2003, hence, according to the Appellant, as per the insurance policy, the vehicle i.e. Tractor No. MTE-4632 and Trolley No.
MWY-6954 involved in the accident was not insured, and

therefore, the direction of the learned Tribunal to the Insurance Company to pay compensation of Rs.7,40,000/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the Petition till its realisation is unjustified and contrary to the factual position in the matter.

4. The learned Counsel for Appellant, in order to justify the grounds 3/6 47.Judg.fa.550.2010.odt raised in the present Appeal, has pointed out from the R & P, which is called in the matter, the original duly stamped policy of the vehicle bearing registration No. MTE-4692 i.e. Tractor involved in the accident.

Bare perusal of the said policy shows that the policy period of the Tractor starts from 13.15 Hrs. on 14/9/2001 upto midnight on 13/9/2002 having Policy No.4926 and an amount of Rs.548/- paid towards premium.
The Appellant further pointed out that the date of collection of premium from the Appellant is 14/9/2001 bearing collection No. 6446.

In the light of this document, submission made by the Appellant found force to the extent that finding recorded by the learned Tribunal that the accident occurred on 16/4/2003 i.e. during the validity period of policy, is perverse in nature.
5. The learned Counsel for Respondents/Claimants vehemently opposed the present Appeal.
He has relied upon the copy of Premium Note dated 9/10/2003 issued by the Officer Incharge of the Appellant/Insurance Company under Section 64 VB of the Insurance Act, 1938.

According to him,
this document clearly demonstrates that collection amount is Rs.548/- dated 14/9/2001, so also the date of commencement of risk is mentioned from 13/9/2002 onwards.

As such, according to him,
the risk as per this document commenced from 13/9/2002 for the period of one year and hence considering 4/6 47.Judg.fa.550.2010.odt the date of accident, the policy issued by the Insurance Company was valid at the time of accident.
6. It is further pointed out by the learned Counsel for Respondents that the Appellant/Insurance Company has raised this objection for the first time before this Court.
No evidence has placed on record by the Insurance Company to substantiate its submission before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.
Therefore, such submission cannot be accepted in the present Appeal.
Hence, according to the learned Counsel for Respondents, the Appeal is devoid of merits and the same deserves to be dismissed.

sentences.text:
In the light of above rival submissions made by the learned Counsel for both sides, one factor cannot be denied in the present Appeal that the learned Tribunal, while delivering the Judgment,
has relied upon the Insurance policy of the offending vehicle i.e. Tractor and Trolley, which was insured with the Appellant/Insurance Company.

As such, by relying on this document, the conclusion was drawn that as per the Premium Note, the risk commenced from 13/9/2002, which means, the policy was in force till 12/9/2003, the Accident took place on 16/4/2003, therefore,
Appellant/Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation amount.
5/6 47.Judg.fa.550.2010.odt 8.

In the light of finding recorded by the Tribunal, submission of the learned Counsel for Respondents cannot be accepted that the document, which Insurance Company has relied upon,
cannot be looked into by this Court in the Appeal.

On the contrary, I am of the considered opinion that the insurance policy, which is a part of the record of Claim Petition, can always be looked into by this Court to verify whether same was properly considered by the learned Tribunal or not.
Therefore, the submission made by the learned Counsel for Respondents is not acceptable.

9. In my opinion, the learned Counsel for Respondents is right in making submission to the extent that the Insurance Company should have entered into the witness-box to clarify the ambiguity in the particulars of premium and the insurance policy which was placed on record before the learned Tribunal.
But, the Insurance Company failed to enter into the witness- box, and therefore, this ambiguity is not clarified in the matter.
Prima facie, it seems that the learned Tribunal has not applied its judicial mind, particularly about the validity period of the insurance policy.
10. In the circumstance, I am of the opinion that this matter needs re-consideration by the learned Tribunal so as to verify the factual position involved in the matter.

The Tribunal will be in a better position to get clear the 6/6 47.Judg.fa.550.2010.odt factual aspect in the matter after granting opportunity to both the parties to place on record their respective documents and the same will be beneficial to all the parties in the matter.
Hence, I proceed to pass following order.
ORDER 1.
The First Appeal is partly allowed.

2. The Judgment and Order dated 1/1/2020 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Nagpur in Claim Petition No. 416/2003 is hereby quashed and set aside.
3.

The Claim Petition is remanded back to the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Nagpur to decide the issue as to whether the offending vehicle was insured with the Appellant/Insurance Company, on the date of accident, along with other issues.

4. The Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Nagpur is requested to decide the Claim Petition at the earliest, by considering the fact that the same is of the year 2003, and in any case, within a period of six months from the date of receipt of record to the Office of the Tribunal.
